x-nous-doc.heading: Completion Actuals Corrections
x-nous-doc.summary: Use `actuals_corrected` when primary evidence proves immutable completion actuals are factually wrong. Append a complete replacement; never edit the raw actuals or emit a partial patch. Each later correction targets the SHA-256 of the currently effective object, forming one linear audit chain.

decision.description: IMP-417 L1. A human ruling. PERMISSIVE by design: only `story` and `event` are required — every one of the 161 real `decision` events on smp carries both — and every other key (`id`, `text`, `reason`, `approved_by`, `subject_work_id`, `relationship`, `ts`, `key_id`, `signature`, …) passes through untouched, so a `decision` without `readiness` is accepted exactly as before this schema existed: an annotation. `readiness` is OPTIONAL and typed-if-present: the machine-readable readiness decision the prose `text` used to carry. When present it is CLOSED (`decision` + `approved_by` required; `partitions` REQUIRED and non-empty iff `decision` is `partition_required`, refused otherwise; `work_id` optional — the work id falls back to `subject_work_id`, then `story`; `tenant_payload_sha256` optional, recorded nowhere but the event because the substrate cannot recompute a tenant digest), the event's `id` is required (it becomes the row's `evidence`, the replay-dedup key) and the event's `ts` is required (it becomes the row's `decided_at` — never the pull's clock). A malformed `readiness` rejects the whole `decision` at pull, naming the field. Persisted append-only to nous.db `readiness_decisions` UNBOUND (`subject='none'`, no digest), so an ingested `ready` records the approval but never makes work claimable on its own.
